chunks: 520 - And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “A man who has no faraṭ will not enter Paradise.”
Then a man among those for whom no child had been born and who had not sent ahead a child said to him: “O Messenger of Allah, does every one of us have a faraṭ?”
He said: “Yes. Indeed, among the faraṭ of the believing man is his brother in Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.أَخَاهُ: his brother, meaning his fellow believer
key_terms.الرَّجُلِ الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believing man, referring here to the faithful person
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; an honorific description of Allah
key_terms.فَرَطٌ: one who goes ahead before another, especially in death, and is counted as preceding them
key_terms.فِي اللَّهِ: for the sake of Allah; a bond grounded in faith and devotion

ai.seo_question: Can a believer have a faraṭ even if they have not lost a child?
ai.summary: The hadith teaches that having someone precede a believer can be a source of spiritual benefit connected to entering Paradise. It broadens the meaning of faraṭ beyond one’s child to include a believing brother in Allah, showing the value of bonds of faith and their significance in the Hereafter.
